eyebrow: Whole organization · SF, Oakland and San Jose
program: Integrated youth employment, education and career support

nutshell.headline: Our best estimate is $508 million per 10 additional SF QALYs.
nutshell.body: Across the Bay Area, including SF, the estimate is $229 million. This costs an entire unrestricted gift, not one SF employment place. Only a modest short-term employment-related health effect is quantified; education, earnings and opportunity may have substantial value outside this health model.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Paid work and integrated support can help transition-age young people build stability and access opportunities.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No local causal QALY effect is established. The small utility gain, marginal spending mix, complete costs and funding additionality are analyst judgments.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Neither central nor favorable assumptions approach $100,000 per 10 QALYs. Verify actual health change and unrestricted-gift use before making a health-based recommendation.

summary.label: SF estimate
summary.detail: Central whole-gift donor estimate; 45% SF residence share is judgmental.

summary.label: Bay estimate
summary.detail: Includes SF and modeled Oakland/San Jose/other Bay beneficiaries; do not add SF again.

summary.label: Gift coverage
summary.detail: Central 70% integrated employment, 30% other provision with unquantified health.

summary.label: Evidence
summary.detail: External adult employment trials do not establish a youth-program QALY effect.

programSection.body: New Door provides paid employment and support, high-school-equivalency education, and career services. The actual portfolio includes San Jose as well as SF and Oakland. Its Vision 2030 strategy is strengthening career-linked pathways; a staffing plan is not evidence of achieved health or a new donor-funded place.

steps.title: Support an integrated employment offer
steps.detail: Paid work, casework, training, supervision, transport and necessary education/transition help are budgeted together.

steps.title: Fund additional education and career services
steps.detail: Separate budget shares cover provision beyond the integrated employment core, not the same support charged twice.

steps.title: Measure health separately from economic progress
steps.detail: Credentials, wages and placements are not converted automatically into health utility or lifetime survival.

programSection.boundary: Central allocation: 70% integrated employment, 15% additional education, 10% additional career services and 5% strategy/reserve/other. These are prospective analyst priors, not audited allocations. All gift cash stays in the numerator; other benefits are unquantified, not assumed absent.

model.headline: A $100,000 gift yields an estimated .001969 SF QALYs, or .004375 across the Bay.
model.body: The central $20,000 complete offered-place allowance funds 3.5 expected six-month employment offers from the $70,000 employment allocation. Fractional offers are expectation accounting, not purchasable slots. The utility average already includes unsuccessful engagement; no second completion or job-placement multiplier is applied.

equation.label: Central SF model
equation.expression: ($70,000 / $20,000) × .005 utility × .5 integrated years × .5 funding additionality × .45 SF share

inputs.label: Integrated employment allocation
inputs.basis: Historical employment spending informs scope but does not establish the next gift’s allocation. Other provision remains costed.

inputs.label: Complete offered-place cost
inputs.basis: Includes wages, casework, training, supervision, transport and allocated shared costs once. Not a quote or mismatched annual-cost/participant ratio.

inputs.label: Average net health utility gain
inputs.basis: Not an imported adult trial coefficient. Average across offered places includes noncompletion; certificates and wages receive no separate health credit.

inputs.label: Integrated health exposure
inputs.basis: All health is within the first year of the offer; exposure integrates onset and decay. No lifetime employment-health tail.

inputs.label: Access caused by the gift
inputs.basis: Services preserved or expanded beyond public/private commitments and accessible alternatives. A deficit alone does not establish this share.

inputs.label: SF residence share
inputs.basis: All modeled recipients are provisionally Bay residents, including San Jose. Accounting location is not beneficiary residence; any non-Bay share needs separate allocation.

model.giftHeading: How much could the estimate change?

sensitivity.headline: $22.22M / 10 SF QALYs
sensitivity.detail: $13.33M per 10 Bay QALYs. Still far above the target; not a confidence limit.

sensitivity.headline: $355.56M SF / $160M Bay
sensitivity.detail: Other central assumptions unchanged. A diagnostic restricted-core comparison, not the central unrestricted portfolio.

sensitivity.headline: Positive ratios double
sensitivity.detail: An illustrative extra $100,000 gives central $1.016B SF and $457.14M Bay. This is not a measured societal-resource estimate.

sensitivity.headline: No positive ratio
sensitivity.detail: No funding additionality or no health gain gives zero. Shared negative utility scales with additionality; independent gift harm can persist even when provision is replaced.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: This is a partial-health portfolio judgment, not measured whole-organization effectiveness or a calibrated probability-weighted mean. The single employment health increment already covers its integrated support; do not add education, career, housing or partner-treatment benefits without distinct causal outcomes and overlap checks. The site’s six-month employment headline and three-month-plus FAQ differ, so the modeled six-month dose needs confirmation.
model.fundingBoundary: Calendar-2025 audited expenses were $6.505M, including $5.079M program expense, and government grants were $1.439M. The operating net-asset decline differs from the total net-asset decline; neither proves a marginal offer. Do not divide calendar-2025 costs by fiscal-2024–25 DCYF outputs. Complete course allowances include overhead and unsuccessful offers. Wages are donor costs but partly transfers in societal accounting; participant labor/time, volunteer inputs and employer output need explicit valuation before subtracting transfers. No full-resource cost or current unfunded slot is verified.

evidence.population: UK adults selected for health-led IPS trials
evidence.result: Small and heterogeneous health-utility findings provide context, not a direct youth effect.
evidence.transfer: The model’s .005 utility is judgment, not a validated transfer or accumulated trial QALYs.

evidence.design: Group Work/JOBS II trial economic evaluation
evidence.result: No mean EQ-5D improvement was reported.
evidence.transfer: Important counterevidence against assuming employment support creates health; not proof all youth programs are ineffective.

evidence.population: New Door youth and career-service users
evidence.result: Paid employment, education support and career pathways are real; programs need not serve disjoint participants.
evidence.transfer: Service existence, jobs and confidence are not causal health outcomes.

evidence.population: New Door’s SF, Oakland, San Jose and additional programs
evidence.result: Finances document a broader organization than the prior single-SF-place model.
evidence.transfer: Historical regional expenditures do not identify prospective prices, resident mix or gift additionality.

reservations: The central and favorable results do not support a sub-$100,000 per 10 QALY claim.
The health-only model omits potentially important educational, economic and community value.
Local utility, duration, marginal allocation and donor additionality are unmeasured judgments.
San Jose is within the actual portfolio; an SF-only employment place is not the whole organization.
Program duration, all-funder costs and current extra capacity remain uncertain.

The official-linked current appeal includes pharmacy-technician training and illustrative wage/transport amounts. These are fundraising examples, not measured QALY effects or complete marginal course prices; their wider earnings and opportunity benefits remain unquantified.
excludedBenefits: Unquantified education, credentials, career progression, wages and longer-run opportunity benefits.
Lifetime mortality or health gains inferred from employment or promotional statistics.
Duplicated support, housing or partner-clinic health effects within the same integrated cohort.
Unpriced employer production, financial transfers or opportunity costs treated as QALYs.
